# Manually rotate static role credentials

The LDAP secrets plugin can rotate LDAP credential for static roles configured
the plugin.

<Tip title="Assumptions">

- You have [set up an `ldap` plugin](/vault/docs/secrets/ldap/setup). 
- You have permission to update LDAP credentials in Vault.

</Tip>

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

@include 'ldap/rotate-creds/cli.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="API" group="api">

@include 'ldap/rotate-creds/api.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="GUI" group="gui">

These steps apply to root-managed and self-managed static roles. Your policy
must grant `read` on `<mount>/static-role/<name>` to open the role and `update`
on `<mount>/rotate-role/<name>` to rotate the credentials. The GUI hides
**Rotate credentials** when you do not have the rotation permission.

1. Log into the Vault GUI using a token with the appropriate permissions.
1. Open **Secrets engines** in the navigation.
1. Select your LDAP mount from the dashboard.
1. Select the **Roles** tab.
1. Select the static role from the dashboard.
1. Click **Manage**.
1. Click **Rotate credentials**.
1. In the **Rotate credentials?** dialog, click **Confirm** to manually rotate
   the credentials and restart the rotation period.

The GUI displays **Credentials successfully rotated.** after a successful
rotation. If you have already revealed the password on the details page, the
GUI refreshes the password after rotation. Otherwise, the GUI does not fetch the
password until you ask to see it.

If you have `read` permission on the `<mount>/static-cred/<name>` path, you can
view the rotated credentials by clicking **Get credentials**. Without this
permission, the GUI hides the **Password** row and the **Get credentials**
button. The **Last Vault rotation** field shows the time of the rotation.

</Tab>

</Tabs>
